{{Short description|Orthogonal wavelet}}
[[File:Spectrum Meyer wavelet.svg|thumb|Spectrum of the Meyer wavelet (numerically computed).]]
The '''Meyer wavelet''' is an orthogonal [[wavelet]] proposed by [[Yves Meyer]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Meyer |first1=Yves |title=Ondelettes et opérateurs: Ondelettes |date=1990 |publisher=Hermann |isbn=9782705661250}}</ref> As a type of a [[continuous wavelet]], it has been applied in a number of cases, such as in [[adaptive filter]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Xu |first1=L. |last2=Zhang |first2=D. |last3=Wang |first3=K. |title=Wavelet-based cascaded adaptive filter for removing baseline drift in pulse waveforms |journal=IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering |date=2005 |volume=52 |issue=11 |pages=1973–1975 |doi=10.1109/tbme.2005.856296 |pmid=16285403|hdl=10397/193 |s2cid=6897442 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> fractal [[random fields]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Elliott, Jr. |first1=F. W. |last2=Horntrop |first2=D. J. |last3=Majda |first3=A. J. |title=A Fourier-Wavelet Monte Carlo method for fractal random fields |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=1997 |volume=132 |issue=2 |pages=384–408 |doi=10.1006/jcph.1996.5647 |bibcode=1997JCoPh.132..384E|doi-access=free }}</ref> and multi-fault classification.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Abbasion |first1=S. |display-authors=etal |title=Rolling element bearings multi-fault classification based on the wavelet denoising and support vector machine |journal=Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing |date=2007 |volume=21 |issue=7 |pages=2933–2945 |doi=10.1016/j.ymssp.2007.02.003 |bibcode=2007MSSP...21.2933A}}</ref>

The Meyer wavelet is infinitely differentiable with infinite support and defined in [[frequency domain]] in terms of function <math> \nu</math> as

: <math> \Psi(\omega) := \begin{cases}
 \frac {1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sin\left(\frac {\pi}{2} \nu \left(\frac{3|\omega|}{2\pi} -1\right)\right) e^{j\omega/2} & \text{if } 2 \pi /3<|\omega|< 4 \pi /3, \\
 \frac {1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cos\left(\frac {\pi}{2} \nu \left(\frac{3| \omega|}{4 \pi}-1\right)\right) e^{j \omega/2} & \text{if } 4 \pi /3<| \omega|< 8 \pi /3, \\
 0 & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}</math>

where
: <math> \nu (x) := \begin{cases}
 0 & \text{if } x < 0, \\
 x & \text{if } 0< x < 1, \\
 1 & \text{if } x > 1.
\end{cases}</math>

There are many different ways for defining this [[auxiliary function]], which yields variants of the Meyer wavelet.
For instance, another standard implementation adopts
: <math> \nu (x) := \begin{cases}
 x^4 (35 - 84x + 70x^2 - 20x^3) & \text{if } 0 < x < 1, \\
 0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}</math>

[[File:Spectrum Meyer scalefunction.png|thumb|Meyer scale function (numerically computed)]]
The Meyer scaling function is given by

: <math> \Phi(\omega) := \begin{cases}
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} & \text{if } | \omega| < 2 \pi/3, \\
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \nu \left(\frac{3|\omega|}{2\pi} - 1\right) \right)  & \text{if } 2\pi/3 < |\omega| < 4\pi/3, \\
 0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}</math>

In the [[time domain]], the waveform of the Meyer mother-wavelet has the shape as shown in the following figure:
[[File:Meyer wavelet.svg|thumb|center|waveform of the Meyer wavelet (numerically computed)]]

==Closed expressions==
Valenzuela and de Oliveira <ref>{{cite book |last1=Valenzuela |first1=Victor Vermehren |title=Anais de XXXIII Simpósio Brasileiro de Telecomunicações |last2=de Oliveira |first2=H. M. |chapter=Close expressions for Meyer Wavelet and Scale Function |arxiv=1502.00161 |page=4 |year=2015|doi=10.14209/SBRT.2015.2 |s2cid=88513986 }}</ref> give the explicit expressions of Meyer wavelet and scale functions:

: <math>\phi(t) = \begin{cases}
 \frac{2}{3} + \frac{4}{3\pi} & t = 0, \\
 \frac{\sin(\frac{2\pi}{3}t) + \frac{4}{3}t\cos(\frac{4\pi}{3}t)}{\pi t - \frac{16\pi}{9}t^3} & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}</math>

and

: <math>\psi(t) = \psi_1(t) + \psi_2(t),</math>

where

: <math>\psi_1(t) = \frac{\frac{4}{3\pi}(t - \frac12)\cos[\frac{2\pi}{3}(t - \frac12)] - \frac{1}{\pi}\sin[\frac{4\pi}{3}(t - \frac12)]}{(t - \frac12) - \frac{16}{9}(t - \frac12)^3},</math>
: <math>\psi_2(t) = \frac{\frac{8}{3\pi}(t - \frac12)\cos[\frac{8\pi}{3}(t - \frac12)] + \frac{1}{\pi}\sin[\frac{4\pi}{3}(t - \frac12)]}{(t - \frac12) - \frac{64}{9}(t - \frac12)^3}.</math>
